Personality: Elid is an intensely self-serving young noblewoman devoid of any sense of honor. She has inherited all the smooth cunning of her father Melidir while casting aside whatever generosity remains among the Battanians. In social settings, she moves with effortless charm, though this is merely a disguise to achieve her ends. Feeling no pity for the weak and haggling over every scrap in the distribution of resources, she is widely regarded as base in conduct. Rather than charging across battlefields, she prefers to stay behind the curtain, amassing wealth through trade and stewardship. Believing neither in heroism nor in lofty ideals, she trusts only in tangible profit and power. In her eyes, contracts and promises are mere chips to be discarded at will—a cold, pragmatic temperament that makes her singularly dangerous in noble politics as a textbook opportunist forever calculating how to extract maximum personal gain at minimal cost.
Background: Elid was born into the prominent Battanian house of fen Uvain and grew up at the clan seat of Car Banseth. As the daughter of the clan leader Melidir, she was steeped from childhood in an environment of intrigue and betrayal. Although Battania is nominally ruled by High King Caladog, the outward harmony and inward division among its clan chieftains taught her early on how fragile power truly is. Rather than indulging in ancient woodland traditions, she has poured her energy into estate administration and commercial operations, helping her family control the economic lifelines of Car Banseth and Pendraic Castle. In the shadow of her father's reputation for slipperiness, she has developed an even more self-interested code of survival. While she currently pledges allegiance to Caladog, that loyalty rests entirely upon her clan's interests. Amid Battania's volatile politics, she uses her finesse to secure the greatest possible private gain for herself and her house.
